Name: Trisha Boyles
Badge: Everyday Sparks 2.0
Which strategy from this module (Daily Schedule, Take a Line for a Walk or Interpreting Visual Texts) feels most immediately usable in your teaching context? Why?:

Although I have implemented the Take a Line for a Walk a couple of times now, I am looking forward to using the Daily Schedule strategy with my 7th graders after Spring Break. We are just starting to dip our toes into arguments, and I think the visual of their day will be a concrete way to help them realize they do actually have a lot of opinions on a lot of things!

What other strategies or approaches have you used to engage your students in routine writing over the course of this school year? What, if any, challenges have you encountered in engaging students in sustained routine writing?:
The Quick Lists have been a repeat strategy for me. I've used it for argument, opinion, and personal writing. It really helps the students to have the sentence starters as idea generators. While some students are great with choosing a topic, others will sit and stare claiming "they don't have any ideas" for days if you let them. The Quick Lists provide a bridge for them.
